h1: AI Product Video Generator From a Link or Photo
lead: This AI product video generator starts from a link or a photo and skips the studio and the crew. You get a product video in a few minutes, for far less than a shoot day.

benefits.d: You do not need editing experience. A few taps are enough to get a full product video out.
Change the sentence, the AI actor, or the setting without rebuilding the whole clip. Drop a word the shop never uses.
A natural voice lets a demo sound like advice from someone who uses the product. A shouty promo voice fights a simple product.

steps.t: Add a Link or a Photo
steps.d: Paste the product page. The photo and the title become the clip. A private page can use one photo instead.
Choose an AI actor who fits the buyer. The hand and the product then read at phone size.
Read the draft. If a line is not something you would say, replace it. The actor speaks the line you leave in.

faq.q: How does a shop get a clip of a product it already lists?
faq.a: Paste the product page you already sell. The photo on that page becomes the clip, and you download it with no watermark after you approve the line.

faq.q: What do I set before a product video is made?
faq.a: Add a link or a photo, pick a frame, then approve the spoken line. You can still change that line after the draft appears.

faq.q: What length should a product video use?
faq.a: Match the length to the action. A short demo can be 6 seconds for 24 credits. A tighter cut is 10 seconds for 40. A standard cut is 15 seconds for 60, and a longer cut is 30 seconds for 120.

faq.q: Can AI create a useful product demo without filming?
faq.a: Yes. The actor can show the product in use while saying the one benefit you kept. You are not renting a set for the shoot.

faq.q: How does a product link become a video?
faq.a: The page supplies the product photo and the claim you already wrote. The spoken clip is built around those two, with an AI actor holding the item.

faq.q: Can I customize the product video after the draft?
faq.a: Yes. Rewrite a sentence, choose a different AI actor, or change the setting. Add your logo when the words are right. The same line can be spoken in another language you sell in.

faq.q: What makes an AI product video different from filming?
faq.a: Filming means reserving a set and a person who can demo the item. Here you start from the product photo. If the render fails, the credits come back.

faq.q: How do I keep the video in my brand's voice?
faq.a: Read the line out loud and rewrite it if it does not sound like the shop. Your logo and colors can sit on the last frame, and shop software you already use can request the same job.

definition.title: What Is an AI Product Video?
paras: An AI product video turns a product page or one photo into a short clip shoppers can judge. An AI actor can hold the item or use it while a script says why to buy.
You approve the line before the clip goes to TikTok, Reels, or the product page. Frames include square 1:1, wide 16:9, tall 9:16, plus 4:3 and 3:4.

reasons.h2: Use Video for a Product That Sells
reasons.lead: A still leaves size, use, and the reason to buy up to the imagination. A product video can carry all three.

items.t: Clean Product Shots in a Hand
items.d: A buyer can judge the size against a palm when an AI actor holds the product. They are not guessing from a plain white photo.
A buyer sees the move when an AI actor uses the product on camera. A still never shows that action.
The product gets the line you already say at the counter, once you approve the wording. A still photo cannot say it.

benefits_lead: You get enough versions to learn which hook deserves the budget, without another shoot day.

reviews.h2: How Shops Use a Product Video
reviews.lead: Four shops start from a ceramic mug and leave with a clip an actor can present.

items.d: They have an AI actor hold the ceramic mug on a counter and say the line they use at checkout. The clip goes on the product page, so they skip a crew for the size demo.
They turn one mug photo into a clip where a hand wraps the cup, so shoppers can judge the size on the listing. They do not book a hand model.
They make a short morning clip of the mug from the photo already on the menu page, with a spoken line, for a phone ad. They skip filming in the cafe before open.
They upload the mug and get an unboxing clip with a spoken line for a paid ad. They check the cup against the one in the box before they post, and they skip a second shoot.
